title: The Recurring Burr
brief: At Meridian Works, burrs on the edge of part 7730 have been found at final inspection in 5 of the last 6 weeks. Each time, the parts were deburred by hand and shipped. Corrective action record CA-118 is marked "closed: operators reminded". You have 12 visit points to interview staff and review records, and to reach a system cause.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Operator: how often the burr appears
Tool change log for the chamfer tool
Tool crib attendant: how tools are replaced
A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: CA-118 lists the cause as "operator error" and the action as "operators reminded". It was closed on day 3 with no effectiveness check, and burrs recurred 4 times after closure.
evidence.whyItMatters: Corrective action must remove the cause and be checked for effectiveness. A reminder addresses people, not the system, and the recurrence shows it did not work.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read the closure section of every corrective action record: cause, action, and evidence that it worked.

evidence.text: Reject data for 6 weeks shows burrs on 2.3 percent of part 7730, all from machine 5. No chart or analysis is attached to CA-118.
evidence.whyItMatters: Data already held could have pointed to machine 5. Analyzing it is an opportunity to improve the investigation.
evidence.missedExplanation: Look at reject data by machine, shift, and date before accepting a cause.

evidence.text: Operator: "It comes and goes. Worse near the end of a tool's life, I think. I report every one in the reject log." The log has 14 entries.
evidence.whyItMatters: The operator reports issues as expected and gives a useful lead.
evidence.missedExplanation: Interviews give leads. Follow them to records.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The operator reported each burr. The issue is not the operator's conduct.

evidence.text: Tool change log: chamfer tool changes for machine 5 are recorded "when worn"; intervals vary from 300 to 1,900 parts. The process sheet sets no tool life.
evidence.whyItMatters: Controlled conditions include defined process settings, such as tool life, where they affect the output.
evidence.missedExplanation: Look for settings that are left to judgment when they affect a characteristic.

evidence.text: Tool crib attendant: "We replace a tool when the setter asks. Stock is always available." Stock count shows 12 chamfer tools.
evidence.whyItMatters: Resources are available. The question is when they are used.
evidence.missedExplanation: This interview leads to the tool change log.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Tool availability is fine; the attendant points you to the log.

evidence.text: Process sheet PS-7730 revision 2 has no edge-break requirement or check frequency for the chamfer, although the drawing calls for "edges broken 0.2 to 0.4 mm".
evidence.whyItMatters: The process instructions must define the checks needed to meet the drawing. A missing in-process check lets burrs travel to final inspection.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare drawing notes with the process sheet line by line.

evidence.text: Setter: "About 6 weeks ago purchasing switched to a cheaper chamfer insert. Nobody asked us to trial it." (interview note 3)
evidence.whyItMatters: A change that affects production should be reviewed before use and its results checked.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask what changed around the time the problem started.

evidence.text: Supplier change notice SCN-41 for the new insert was received 7 weeks ago and filed in purchasing. No technical review or trial is recorded.
evidence.whyItMatters: Changes in externally provided products should be checked for their effect on conformity before acceptance.
evidence.missedExplanation: Follow a change to its approval record.

evidence.text: Operator deburrs 40 parts by hand with a scraper, then re-inspects 5 at random. Rework is authorized on the reject ticket.
evidence.whyItMatters: Authorized rework with re-inspection is acceptable correction of nonconforming output.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The rework is authorized and verified. The problem is that it keeps being needed, which is a cause question, not a control failure at this station.

evidence.text: Coolant nozzles on machine 5 are slightly misaligned, but the coolant flow log shows normal flow and the setter checks alignment each shift.
evidence.whyItMatters: A minor visual impression without effect on the process is not evidence of a nonconformity.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Flow is recorded as normal and alignment is checked. Do not build a cause from an impression.

evidence.text: Preventive maintenance on machine 5 is complete for the quarter; spindle runout was measured at 0.004 mm, within limit.
evidence.whyItMatters: The machine is maintained, which rules out one possible cause.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence that narrows the cause.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Maintenance is current. Ruling causes out is part of good analysis.

evidence.text: The insert supplier is on the approved supplier list with a current evaluation.
evidence.whyItMatters: The supplier is approved; the gap is the review of the product change, not the supplier's status.

evidence.text: Training record for new setter badge 318 shows machine setup training but no record of training on edge-break checks.
evidence.whyItMatters: Competence should cover the checks a role performs. This is a gap to close rather than evidence of a failure.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check that training records cover the checks the process needs.

decisions.prompt: Which statement best describes the system cause?
options: An untrialed insert change met a process with no defined tool life and no in-process edge check, so burrs went undetected until final inspection
Machine 5 is worn out and must be replaced
The burr cannot be prevented, so hand deburring should continue
decisions.rationale: The evidence links the timing to the insert change, and shows that the process had no tool life and no in-process check. Those are system conditions that apply to anyone running the job.

containment: Increase edge checks on part 7730 from machine 5 until the cause is removed
correction: Deburr and re-inspect affected parts under the existing authorized rework
cause: No review of the insert change, no defined tool life, and no in-process edge-break check
corrective: Trial and approve tool changes through change control; set tool life and an in-process edge check in PS-7730
Reopen CA-118 with the system cause and a defined effectiveness check
effectiveness: Track burr rejects on part 7730 for eight weeks after the change, with a target of zero

debriefText.found: You moved from symptom to system: the insert change, the missing tool life, and the missing in-process check.
debriefText.missed: In a root cause case, ask "what changed?" and "what in the process allows this?" before accepting any answer that names a person.
debriefText.falseFinding: Authorized rework and a cosmetic impression are not causes. Test every suspected cause against a record.
